Also track a planner improvement so deferred work does not distort current-lane progress reporting.

phase.title: Gameplay responsiveness and content-driven board UX
phase.goal: Make the playable KAPLAY game feel responsive and readable again: move expensive turn resolution behind a worker-ready sync-then-dispatch turn runner, keep the engine deterministic, extend initiative/speed-aware queue behavior from the existing runtime meters, improve room/entity/encounter legibility on the navigation board with stronger sprite/icon language, and use smoke/unit/perf coverage to keep the gameplay loop reviewable during the human feedback cycle.
phase.requirements: [User direction: gameplay focus returns now; keep architecture organized; use Playwright; move expensive computation off the main thread where practical]
phase.depends: Phase 63 no longer blocks local authoring/import/publish, so active work can return to the game. Build on Phase 46 human-playable UX, Phase 48 polish, and Phase 62 engine decomposition.
phase.plans: `64-01` add a dedicated turn-runner seam in `packages/kaplay-demo`, move UI-side turn execution toward worker/off-main-thread operation with explicit worker sync + action dispatch, expose pending-turn/debug timing state, extend the initiative/speed queue from the current engine meters instead of introducing a second scheduler, improve room/entity hover and encounter clarity with boss-visible/full-cell board language plus sprite portraits, simplify the spellbook to a pool-first assignment model, and add smoke/unit/perf coverage plus explicit turn-budget guardrails for the playable navigation loop. `64-02` landed the room-focus navigation slice: remove fallback combat rooms from generation, route combat strictly through encounters, give treasure/training/rune forge their own map-or-room tabbed center view with concrete room actions, and replace bracketed pseudo-hotkeys with keycap/icon-driven affordances. `64-03` landed the loadout-menu clarity slice: bag and spellbook menus now use icon-first tabs, top-pinned context actions, stronger selected-card borders, and rarity-driven item/spell cues so the current gameplay shell reads more like a deliberate RPG menu than a debug grid. `64-04` landed the navigation-feed/input cleanup slice: the bottom panel is now a gamer-facing live feed, room-focus tabs use `M` and `R`, navigation actions use explicit `Space`/`V`/`X` keycaps, and hidden action slots no longer leave shadow bars behind. `64-05` landed the treasure/dialogue/readability follow-up: treasure-room search now stays reward-first, dialogue choice continuation drops back to navigation instead of trapping the overlay, header controls render as keycap legends, and text contrast is stronger across the live shell. `64-06` added a design-vs-implementation audit slice that turned the next visible gameplay gaps into concrete work. `64-07` is now landed: command-board/menu rows show real keycaps instead of cursor/debug selection language, duplicate detail headings are gone, and the shell uses cleaner control copy. `64-08` is now landed: normal bag flow no longer exposes sell or treasure-container semantics, generated gameplay loot resolves to canonical sprites/placeholders, and surfaced item/spell equipment identity is more consistent. `64-09` is now landed: livestream is a persistent toggle with per-turn mana/Fame behavior, feed/action labels reflect that stateful model, and shared overlay/rendering cleanup reduced maintenance drift while improving readability. Remaining phase-64 work is the larger worker/perf/smoke lane plus broader authored media expansion beyond the surfaced fallback coverage shipped here.
